cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Would you sell your signed guitar so we can replace the fridge? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I queued all night for that signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then let's price it properly. Those hours should buy us an ice maker.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sell the case. The guitar stays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the case. You can still tell the queue story while I photograph the guitar.

mechanism: A confidently manages a sale or donation but gives B recognition or control to keep B willing to surrender the valued object.
confusable: Distinguish coercive confiscation from tailoring surrender to the value B actually names; confidence must depend on consent, not merely asserted rank.
comparison: Only-won medal needs public recognition retained; signed guitar needs years-of-memory value and price control respected.
seedUse: Canonical medal/guitar seeds identify what matters to B; S02 adaptations should preserve that emotional value while still pursuing actual surrender.
